recent_posts.title: Phoenix LiveView widgets with hooks: a reusable pattern
recent_posts.summary: A detailed pattern for building self-contained, stateful widgets in Phoenix LiveView using attach_hook/4, function components, and plain structs stored in socket.assigns. The approach solves limitations of LiveComponents (no handle_info, no handle_params) and embedded LiveViews (separate processes, string-only session). Each widget module encapsulates a state struct, an assign_component/n setup function, a pure render/1 function component, and optional hook callbacks for events, PubSub messages, and URL params. A full chat widget example demonstrates event namespacing, multi-instance support via assign keys, PubSub integration, URL-driven state, and a memory trade-off with LiveView streams. The parent LiveView needs only two lines to mount and render the widget.

recent_posts.title: Embedded Elixir sound controller with Nerves and Arduino
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of building a DIY sound controller using Elixir/Nerves on Raspberry Pi with two Arduino boards and 10 sensors. The system generates OSC messages for PureData and focuses on fault tolerance: each sensor runs in an isolated process via DynamicSupervisor, timeouts trigger fallback values, disconnected sensors are detected via hardware voltage dividers, and three temperature sensors use triple modular redundancy (TMR) voting to filter bad readings. The architecture allows swapping sensors or output devices without changing core logic, making it suitable for art installations, DIY synthesizers, and experimental IoT deployments.

recent_posts.title: Phoenix scopes vs authorization: what developers need to know
recent_posts.summary: Phoenix 1.8 introduces Scopes as a structured container for request context (current user, tenant, permissions) that gets passed into domain/context functions to enforce data boundaries. The post explains how mix phx.gen.auth generates a default scope struct, wires it into the browser pipeline via a plug, and provides a matching on_mount hook for LiveView. It then covers how Permit.Phoenix builds on top of Phoenix Scopes to add repeatable authorization enforcement across controllers and LiveViews, handling permission checks, resource preloading, and unauthorized outcomes consistently. A decision guide helps developers choose between raw scopes alone versus adding Permit.Phoenix based on complexity of access rules.

recent_posts.title: Six React Native development companies compared for business use
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of six React Native development agencies, with guidance on how to evaluate vendors. Key selection criteria include open-source contributions, brownfield integration experience, and technical communication skills. The six companies profiled are Curiosum (Elixir + React Native stack), Software Mansion (animations and multimedia), Callstack (enterprise scaling), Infinite Red (US-based consulting), Miquido (full-cycle with AI), and Droids On Roids (transparency and visual quality). Each entry covers location, best-fit use cases, and notable strengths.

recent_posts.title: Permit.Absinthe 0.2: Absinthe GraphQL authorization for Elixir
recent_posts.summary: Permit.Absinthe v0.2.0 graduates from proof-of-concept to production-ready, bringing the Permit authorization library's load-and-authorize pattern to Absinthe GraphQL in Elixir. Key additions include a rich set of customization options on the `permit` macro: `base_query` and `finalize_query` for Ecto query control, `fetch_subject` for custom user extraction, `handle_unauthorized`/`handle_not_found` error callbacks, a custom `loader` for non-Ecto sources, and a `wrap_authorized` post-authorization hook. The release also adds custom ID field support, a Dataloader integration via `authorized_dataloader/3` for batched association loading, and a reference table to help developers choose between resolver, middleware, directive, and Dataloader integration points. The schema-wide hydrator remains a work in progress. The API is still 0.x with possible breaking changes before 1.0.

recent_posts.title: Design-Backed Pitch Deck for investors: clean, clear, credible slides
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide for early-stage founders on building an effective investor pitch deck. Covers the core mindset (deck as a movie trailer, not the full film), what investors actually care about at pre-seed/seed stage (team, problem, solution, market, traction, business model, and the ask), and design principles (clean, minimal, consistent). Key advice includes keeping decks to 10–15 slides, using bottom-up market sizing, leading with traction, avoiding exit strategy slides, and prioritizing clarity over flashy visuals.

recent_posts.title: Startup branding after MVP: refresh without a full rebrand
recent_posts.summary: Post-MVP startups often face inconsistent branding across channels without needing a full rebrand. A brand refresh (evolution) differs from a rebrand (revolution) – choose refresh when your product has outpaced your branding. The Minimum Viable Branding approach includes a core message, logo, color scheme, voice guide, and social templates. Use the Keep-Fix-Upgrade framework to audit existing assets: keep aligned elements, fix inconsistencies, upgrade what's holding you back. Start by revisiting positioning and messaging before visual changes. Create a simple design system with locked-down colors, fonts, and UI components for consistency. Communicate changes transparently to early users and team members who supported your journey.

recent_posts.title: Build maintainable Elixir apps with Ash Framework
recent_posts.summary: Ash Framework helps organize Elixir business logic by centralizing domain rules in Resources instead of scattering them across modules. The framework uses a declarative approach where you define what your system is and what it can do through Resources and Actions. Key features include automatic database migration generation from resource definitions, built-in CRUD actions with code interfaces, custom validations, calculations for derived data, and filtering through action arguments. Resources serve as the single source of truth, containing attributes, actions, validations, and business rules in one place, making applications more maintainable and consistent as they grow.

recent_posts.title: Curiosum becomes main sponsor of Hologram
recent_posts.summary: Curiosum announces its main sponsorship of Hologram, an Elixir framework that transpiles Elixir code to JavaScript for browser-side execution. Hologram's creator, Bart Blast, joins Curiosum's team while maintaining full project ownership. The framework addresses Phoenix LiveView's limitations by enabling zero-latency client-side interactions, reducing server load, and eliminating the need for manual JavaScript. Curiosum will provide strategic, engineering, consulting, and financial support to accelerate Hologram's development and adoption.

recent_posts.title: Do you need a design system yet? A startup’s guide to consistent digital product.
recent_posts.summary: Design systems provide reusable UI components and guidelines that speed up development and ensure consistency, but startups must weigh the investment against their current priorities. Early-stage companies rapidly pivoting or hunting for product-market fit may find formal design systems premature and constraining. However, teams experiencing UI inconsistencies, multiple designers/developers, or repetitive copy-paste work should consider a minimal approach: borrow existing frameworks, build components incrementally during regular feature work, start with basic styles (colors, typography, spacing), and evolve the system as the product matures rather than treating it as a separate project.
